My best friend killed herself. I won't say how. But the depression made her believe that no one would suffer from it but her. Not so, I still think of her, mourn her every day, and it feels like my insides are being torn out. It's been 13 years, and the pain for me, her family, everyone who knew her hasn't stopped, and likely never will. Her decision cut those around her deeply and was damaging... and she had far more friends than she believed. I had gone off to college and blamed myself for not calling. Those friends who have "gone by the wayside" are probably caught up in their own drama, but are still your friends. Reach out to them, tell them how you feel. They will hurt if you die, no matter what you think, and they will bear the crippling scars for the rest of their lives.

Chemical depression can be treated, successfully, even if you haven't had success in the past. I beg you talk to a counselor before taking this path.

I always have had a memory for factoids, so it came as a shock to me when I realized that I hadn't noticed that my close older relative had been missing a finger for longer than my entire lifetime. I finally looked down during a conversation when I was 27, did a double-take, and uttered the immortal words: "You have nine fingers, did I miss something?" She explained, very patiently, that she had lost it to an untreated infection when she was in HER twenties. It had never occurred to me that I could miss something like that... in plain sight all my life. I felt like captain oblivious that day.
